q: In a code, DOCTOR is written as EPDUPS. Using the same code, how is NURSE written?
x: Each letter is replaced by the next letter of the alphabet (D→E, O→P…). So N→O, U→V, R→S, S→T, E→F gives OVSTF.

q: In a code, HEART is written as TRAEH. Using the same code, how is BLOOD written?
x: The code simply writes the word backwards: HEART becomes TRAEH. Written backwards, BLOOD becomes DOOLB.

q: In a code, LUNG is written as JSLE. Using the same code, how is LIVER written?
x: Each letter moves two places back: L→J, U→S, N→L, G→E. So L→J, I→G, V→T, E→C, R→P gives JGTCP; NKXGT moves forward instead.

q: In a code, CAB = 6 and BAD = 7, where each letter stands for its position in the alphabet. Using the same rule, what is FACE?
x: The code adds the letter positions: C(3)+A(1)+B(2) = 6 and B(2)+A(1)+D(4) = 7. So FACE = 6+1+3+5 = 15. Multiplying fails for BAD (2×1×4 = 8).

q: In a code language, "pit na sod" means "study hard daily", "na lam ret" means "work hard always" and "sod ret kip" means "daily always win". What is the code for "work"?
x: "hard" is common to the first two sentences, so hard = na; "always" is common to the last two, so always = ret. The only word left in the second sentence is lam = work.

q: In a code, each letter is replaced by the letter in the same position from the end of the alphabet, so CELL is written as XVOO. How is GENE written?
x: A↔Z, B↔Y and so on: the two positions always add up to 27. G(7)→T(20), E(5)→V(22), N(14)→M(13), so GENE becomes TVMV.

q: In a code, BAD is written as CCG and FIG is written as GKJ. Using the same code, how is CAT written?
x: The first letter moves 1 place forward, the second 2 places and the third 3 places (B→C, A→C, D→G). So C→D, A→C, T→W gives DCW.

q: In a code, MAT is written as NBU. Using the same code, a word is written as TFF. What is the word?
x: MAT→NBU shows each letter moves one place forward. To decode, move each letter one place back: T→S, F→E, F→E gives SEE. UGG wrongly moves forward again.

q: Ali, Sara, Hamza, Ayesha and Bilal sit in seats 1 to 5 in a row, numbered from left to right. Ali is in seat 3, Hamza is in seat 1, and Sara is not next to Ali. If Ayesha is in seat 4, who is in seat 2?
x: Sara cannot be in seat 2 or 4 (next to Ali), so she is in seat 5. With Ayesha in seat 4, the only seat left for Bilal is seat 2.

q: Sara is taller than Ali. Hamza is taller than Sara. Bilal is shorter than Ali. Ayesha is taller than Bilal. If Ayesha is the tallest of the five, who is the second tallest?
x: The clues give the chain Hamza > Sara > Ali > Bilal. With Ayesha at the top, the full order is Ayesha, Hamza, Sara, Ali, Bilal, so Hamza is second.

q: Five meetings P, Q, R, S and W are held one per day from Monday to Friday. Q is on Wednesday. P is on a day before Q. R is on the day immediately after S. If W is on Monday, on which day is P?
x: With Q on Wednesday and W on Monday, P must be on Tuesday, the only free day before Wednesday. S and R then take Thursday and Friday.

q: Hamza scored 60 marks in a test. Sara scored 5 marks less than Hamza, and Ali scored 15 marks more than Sara. Bilal's score was exactly halfway between Ali's and Hamza's. What did Bilal score?
x: Sara = 60 − 5 = 55, so Ali = 55 + 15 = 70. Bilal is halfway between 70 and 60, which is 65.

q: Ali, Sara, Hamza and Fatima each own a different pet: a cat, a parrot, a fish and a rabbit. Ali does not own the cat. Sara owns the fish or the rabbit. Hamza does not own the parrot. If Fatima owns the cat and Sara does not own the rabbit, which pet does Hamza own?
x: Fatima has the cat and Sara must have the fish. The parrot and rabbit remain for Ali and Hamza; Hamza cannot have the parrot, so he has the rabbit.

q: Ali, Sara, Hamza, Ayesha, Bilal and Fatima sit around a round table, equally spaced and facing the centre. Ali sits opposite Bilal. Sara sits immediately to the right of Ali. Hamza sits next to Bilal. If Fatima sits opposite Sara, who sits opposite Hamza?
x: Fatima, opposite Sara, takes one of the two seats beside Bilal, so Hamza takes the other. That seat is directly opposite the seat on Ali's other side, which only Ayesha can fill.

q: Five runners finish a race with no ties. Ali finishes before Sara. Hamza finishes immediately after Ali. Ayesha finishes before Ali. Bilal does not finish last. If Ayesha finishes second, in which position does Bilal finish?
x: Ali comes after Ayesha (2nd) but cannot be 4th, or Hamza would be 5th with no place left for Sara. So Ali is 3rd, Hamza 4th, Sara 5th, and Bilal takes 1st.

q: Ali, Sara, Hamza, Ayesha and Bilal sit in seats 1 to 5 in a row, numbered from left to right. Hamza is in seat 5. Sara sits immediately to the left of Hamza, and Ali immediately to the left of Sara. Ayesha is not in seat 1. Who is in seat 1?
x: Hamza 5, Sara 4 and Ali 3. Seats 1 and 2 remain for Ayesha and Bilal; Ayesha is not in seat 1, so Bilal is.

q: Ali, Sara, Hamza, Ayesha and Bilal each study a different subject: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, English or Maths. Hamza studies Chemistry and Ayesha studies Biology. Ali studies neither English nor Maths. Bilal does not study English. Who studies English?
x: Physics, English and Maths are left for Ali, Sara and Bilal. Ali can only take Physics; Bilal cannot take English, so he takes Maths and Sara studies English.

q: Five lectures, Anatomy, Botany, Chemistry, Physics and Zoology, are held one per day from Monday to Friday. Chemistry is on Wednesday. Botany is the day immediately after Anatomy. Physics is not on Monday or Friday. Zoology is after Chemistry. On which day is Botany?
x: Anatomy–Botany must be Monday–Tuesday or Thursday–Friday. Thursday–Friday leaves no day after Wednesday for Zoology, so Botany is on Tuesday (Physics Thursday, Zoology Friday).

q: Hamza is taller than Ali. Sara is shorter than Ali. Bilal is taller than Hamza. Ayesha is shorter than Sara. Who is the shortest?
x: Putting the clues together gives Bilal > Hamza > Ali > Sara > Ayesha, so Ayesha is the shortest.

q: A building has five floors, numbered 1 (lowest) to 5. Ali, Sara, Hamza, Ayesha and Bilal each live on a different floor. Hamza lives on floor 1. Ayesha lives on an even-numbered floor. Sara lives above Ayesha but not on floor 5. Bilal lives directly above Ali. Who lives on floor 5?
x: If Ayesha were on floor 4, Sara would have to be on 5, which is not allowed; so Ayesha is on 2. Bilal directly above Ali needs two adjacent free floors, which forces Sara 3, Ali 4, Bilal 5.

q: Ali, Sara and Hamza are a doctor, an engineer and a teacher, one each, and live in Lahore, Karachi and Peshawar, one each. The doctor lives in Karachi. Sara lives in Peshawar. Hamza is not the doctor. The engineer does not live in Peshawar. What is Sara's profession?
x: Sara lives in Peshawar, so she is neither the doctor (Karachi) nor the engineer (not Peshawar). She must be the teacher.

q: Ali, Sara, Hamza, Ayesha, Bilal and Fatima sit around a round table, equally spaced and facing the centre. Ali sits opposite Sara. Hamza sits immediately to the right of Ali. Fatima sits opposite Hamza. Ayesha does not sit next to Sara. Who sits immediately to the left of Ali?
x: Fatima, opposite Hamza, sits next to Sara. The two remaining seats are on Sara's other side and on Ali's left; Ayesha cannot sit beside Sara, so she sits on Ali's left.

q: In a test, no two students got the same marks. Hamza scored more than Bilal but less than Ayesha. Sara scored more than Ayesha. Ali scored more than exactly one of the other four. Who came third?
x: The clues give Sara > Ayesha > Hamza > Bilal. Ali beats exactly one person, so he is fourth and Bilal fifth, leaving Hamza third.

q: Four boxes P, Q, R and S are stacked one on top of another. Q is directly above S. P is neither at the top nor at the bottom. R is somewhere below P. Which box is at the top?
x: If P were third from the bottom, the free positions would not let Q sit directly on S. So P is second, R is at the bottom, S third and Q at the top.

q: Ali, Sara, Hamza and Fatima each like a different fruit: mango, apple, banana or guava. Sara likes banana. Ali likes neither mango nor guava. Fatima does not like mango. Which fruit does Fatima like?
x: Ali can only like apple (banana is Sara's). Neither Ali, Sara nor Fatima likes mango, so Hamza does, leaving guava for Fatima.

q: Ali, Sara, Hamza and Ayesha come from Lahore, Quetta, Multan and Karachi, and study Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy and Nursing (one each). The student from Quetta studies Pharmacy. Sara is from Multan. Hamza studies Dentistry and is not from Karachi. Ayesha does not study Nursing and is not from Quetta. What does Sara study?
x: Hamza cannot be from Quetta (Pharmacy), Multan or Karachi, so he is from Lahore; Ayesha is then from Karachi and Ali from Quetta (Pharmacy). Ayesha is left with Medicine, so Sara studies Nursing.

q: Ali, Sara, Hamza and Fatima sit at a square table, one on each side, facing the centre. Ali sits opposite Sara. Hamza sits on Ali's left. Who sits on Sara's left?
x: Sara faces Ali, so her left is on the opposite side to Ali's left. Hamza is on Ali's left, so the person on Sara's left is the remaining one, Fatima.

q: A doctor sees five patients, Ali, Sara, Hamza, Ayesha and Bilal, one after another. Sara is seen third. Bilal is seen immediately before Ali. Hamza is seen after Sara. Ayesha is not seen last. Who is seen fourth?
x: Bilal–Ali cannot be 4th–5th, or Hamza would have no place after Sara, so they are 1st and 2nd. Ayesha is not last, so Ayesha is 4th and Hamza 5th.

q: Sara has twice as many books as Ali. Hamza has 3 more books than Sara. Together the three have 28 books. How many books does Hamza have?
x: Let Ali have x books: x + 2x + (2x + 3) = 28, so 5x = 25 and x = 5. Sara has 10 and Hamza has 13.

q: Ali, Sara, Hamza, Ayesha, Bilal and Fatima sit in seats 1 to 6 in a row, numbered from left to right. Sara and Bilal sit at the two ends. Ali sits immediately to the right of Sara. Fatima sits immediately to the left of Bilal. Hamza does not sit next to Ali. Who is in seat 4?
x: Ali is to Sara's right, so Sara is in seat 1, Ali 2, Bilal 6 and Fatima 5. Hamza cannot be in seat 3 (next to Ali), so he is in seat 4.

q: Ali, Sara, Hamza, Ayesha and Bilal each do night duty on one day from Monday to Friday. Hamza's duty is exactly two days after Ali's. Sara is not on duty on Monday. Bilal's duty is the day immediately after Sara's. Who is on duty on Wednesday?
x: Testing Ali on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday, only Ali Monday leaves two adjacent free days (Thursday–Friday) for Sara and Bilal. So Ali Mon, Ayesha Tue, Hamza Wed, Sara Thu, Bilal Fri.
